description.value: The study explored neural correlates of preparatory control associated with the intention to suppress or cognitively reappraise upcoming negative emotions, as well as neural activity during the subsequent emotion-regulation performance.

spans.text: Altogether, the primary goal of this study was to explore neural correlates of preparatory control associated with the purpose to suppress or reappraise upcoming negative emotions.

design.value: Event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging was recorded while participants completed an emotion-regulation paradigm involving proactive preparation followed by suppression, reappraisal, or appraisal of negative high-arousing images.

spans.text: Using event-related fMRI, we investigated neural correlates while participants were anticipating reappraisal or suppression (proactive, cue phase), as well as while they were applying these ERS (reactive, target phase), all within the context of negative, high-arousing emotions.
